claims.text: A machine-learning-based potential can substantially reduce the computational cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties for high-entropy alloys.
The machine-learning potential can maintain accuracy while reducing computational cost.
The proposed method applies to both solid and fluid states of high-entropy alloys.
The intervention consists of training and deploying a machine-learning-based interatomic potential.
The machine-learning potential is trained on ab initio calculations for a subset of high-entropy systems.
The relevant thermodynamic treatment must retain vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling.
The machine-learning potential captures the essential interactions and correlations in the system.
Capturing the essential interactions and correlations enables efficient and accurate calculation of phase free energies and thermodynamic properties.
The method will reduce computational cost by a factor of 5–10 relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The method will reduce computational cost by a factor of 2–5 relative to TOR-TILD.
The method will achieve 90–95% fidelity in phase free energies and derived observables.
The proposed applicability domain comprises high-entropy systems with 3–6 principal components.
The proposed applicability domain spans temperatures from 500 to 2000 K, particularly near and above the phase-transition temperature.
Accuracy may depend on the quality and diversity of the training dataset.
The potential may have limited transferability to unseen systems.
The hypothesis is falsified if the mean absolute error in phase free energies exceeds 10% or the mean absolute error in derived observables exceeds 15%.
